title: Using tangent to find the height of a tree
examples: How do you find the height of a tree with trigonometry?
What is an angle of elevation?
Why use tan to find a height?

explain.say: A mango tree at your school in Chennai is too tall for a tape measure. But you can find its height with one angle! First, walk 10 metres away from the tree, and measure that distance along the ground.

explain.say: Now look up at the very top of the tree and measure the angle up from the ground. This is called the angle of elevation. Here it is 40 degrees. A clinometer or a phone app can measure it.

stages.ask: How do you measure the angle of elevation?

stages.label: Use tangent
stages.note: tan 40° = height ÷ 10

explain.say: Picture the triangle. The ground is next to the angle, so it is the adjacent side. The tree is across from the angle, so it is the opposite side. Which ratio uses opposite and adjacent?
TOA, tangent! Tangent is opposite over adjacent. So tan 40 degrees equals the height divided by 10. A calculator says tan 40 degrees is about 0.84.

explain.say: So the height is 10 times 0.84, about 8.4 metres. You did it! Wow: surveyors in the 1800s worked out the height of Mount Everest with angles like this, from over 100 kilometres away. Challenge: 20 metres from a tower, the angle is 45 degrees. How tall is it?

faq.q: How do you measure the angle of elevation?
faq.a: Stand still, look up at the top of the object and measure the angle between the flat ground and your line of sight. A clinometer or a phone app can do this.
asks: What is an angle of elevation?

faq.a: You know the side next to the angle, the ground, and want the side across from it, the tree. Tangent links opposite and adjacent.

faq.q: What if I measure from eye level?
faq.a: Then the triangle starts at your eyes, not the ground. Work out the height above your eyes, then add your eye height, for example 1.5 metres.
It is exactly 1. So at 45 degrees the height equals the distance: 20 metres away means a 20 metre tower.
In the Great Trigonometric Survey of India, surveyors measured angles to the peak from several stations over 100 kilometres away, and used trigonometry to calculate its height.

facts: Everest's height was first calculated in the 1850s by the Great Trigonometric Survey of India, using angles measured from distant stations.

quiz.say: You stand 15 metres from a wall. The angle to its top is 45 degrees. How tall is the wall?
quiz.why: tan 45 degrees is 1, so the height equals the distance, 15 metres.

wrong.1: 7.5 halves the distance for no reason.
